governance_restrictions.evidence: E2 regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: 'restricted'; 'Access to every data modality is controlled.'

datasets_shared_available_for_reuse.evidence: distribution_formats populated (OMOP CDM tables, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst, OHNLP-tokenized text); third_party_sharing.is_shared: true ('The dataset is made available beyond the contributing consortium under controlled access'). Per the ambiguity rule, approval-gated enclave access defaults to applicable.

software_tools_produced.evidence: external_resources (E10) references the 'CHoRUS for Equitable AI GitHub organization (https://github.com/chorus-ai), housing 28 repositories of tooling, validated semantic mappings, standard operating procedures, and project management overviews'

data_collection_identified_and_shared.evidence: acquisition_methods (3 entries) and collection_mechanisms (6 entries) populated; datasets-shared condition met

publication_identified_and_shared.evidence: No citation field; external_resources lists the project website, GitHub organization, NIH RePORTER grant record, a Bridge2AI program page, and a training-program webinar — none is a publication reference. existing_uses mentions 'training activities and publications' generically without identifying any citable work. Gates Element 10 sub-element 2 only.

issues_detected.description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true (patient-level ICU/PICU/NICU records explicitly including minors and neonates) but no IRB approval or reviewing committee is documented: ethical_reviews.source_caveats states the sources 'do not name a reviewing body, nor report an institutional review board determination or approval number for the dataset, so reviewing_organization is left empty'. The gap is honestly flagged as a source gap rather than fabricated over, but the human-subjects consistency expectation still fails.
issues_detected.recommendation: Obtain and document IRB/ethics approvals (or the applicable waiver determinations) covering the 14 data-acquisition hospitals, with protocol numbers and reviewing institutions.

issues_detected.description: involves_human_subjects=true but informed_consent is entirely absent; at_risk_populations.source_caveats confirms 'The sources do not describe guardian consent or assent procedures for the pediatric and neonatal admissions represented in the data', and the record-level source_caveats lists 'consent documentation' among slots omitted because nothing is stated in the bundle. For retrospective EHR data a waiver of consent is the likely mechanism, but it is not documented.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document the consent basis — most plausibly an IRB-approved waiver of informed consent for retrospective records — including its application to pediatric and neonatal admissions.

issues_detected.description: No DOI or RRID; the id (https://chorus4ai.org/#chorus-dataset) is self-minted — source_caveats admits 'The dataset identifier is a fragment minted on the attested project URL and does not correspond to any anchor the source publishes.' For a released dataset this materially limits citability and cross-referencing.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mint a DOI (e.g., via DataCite through the hosting platform) and register an RRID for the resource.

issues_detected.description: A released dataset (status: 'Released under controlled access while assembly continues') has no version number, version access method, errata, recommended citation, or formal release date; source_caveats states 'No DOI, recommended citation, version identifier, dataset license, consent documentation, file counts, total size, compression, or direct download URL is stated anywhere in the bundle.'
issues_detected.recommendation: Assign explicit version numbers to enclave releases, publish a changelog, and record the initial release date.

issues_detected.description: license_and_use_terms describes the access mechanism ('all participants must sign a licensing agreement before gaining access') but not the substantive reuse permissions (publication rights, redistribution, derivative-model rights), so a prospective user cannot determine what reuse is allowed. The software/data licensing distinction (MIT/Apache-2.0 for repositories vs signed agreement for data) is correctly drawn.
issues_detected.recommendation: Summarize the key terms of the data licensing agreement (permitted uses, publication policy, re-identification prohibition, enclave export policy).

issues_detected.description: Maintainer contact email domain 'mgh.havard.edu' is a typo in the published source; the datasheet transcribes it exactly and flags it ('transcribed exactly as published and apparently containing a typographical error in the domain'). The Bridge2AI program page is given as 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' without a URL scheme, also transcribed as published. Neither is an evaluator-detected fabrication; both are minor.
issues_detected.recommendation: Confirm the correct contact address with the source and normalize the Bridge2AI URL with an https:// scheme.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata or data dictionary; is_tabular=false is semantically correct for a multimodal dataset and OMOP CDM conformance implies table structure, but users get no column-level guidance for the ~1.6 billion EHR rows. The source-level per-modality metadata-schema status could not be reconstructed from the garbled webinar table, which the record transparently declines to assert.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variable metadata for the OMOP tables in use (including the nursing-flowsheet schema extensions) or link the published per-modality metadata schemas as they are released.

semantic_insights: Exemplary source-conflict handling: record-level source_caveats reconciles the 50,000 (tier-2 project site) vs 45,000+ (tier-4 webinar) admission counts by explicit source tiering, and separately notes that 7,642 radiology admissions and 1,000 de-identified images 'count different units and both are recorded'.

The garbled webinar modality table is handled with unusual epistemic care: per-modality metadata status is not asserted at all, and the two entries attributed on column order alone ('OMOP schema with extensions' to nursing flowsheets, 'PhysioNet schema extended' to waveform telemetry) carry local caveats in the affected subsets.

Correctly scopes the MIT License to the CHoRUS software repositories rather than the controlled-access clinical dataset — 'The MIT License statement applies to the CHoRUS GitHub project rather than to the dataset' — a distinction many datasheets get wrong.

Deidentification methods are semantically appropriate per modality: OHNLP tokenization for free text with full notes retained locally at sites, PACS imaging de-identification (with CTP-deid and a privacy scan tool named), and re-identification-limiting transforms, all reinforced by controlled enclave access.

The absence of a download_url is semantically correct for an enclave model: OMOP and telemetry data reside in the cloud enclave, trainees are provisioned compute on the Bridge2AI Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud, and the registration/licensing/.edu access path is fully documented in data_governance.

NIH award OT2OD032701 (project number 1OT2OD032701-01, RePORTER application ID 10472824) matches the NIH [Type][Institute][Serial] pattern and is used consistently across creators, funders, and external_resources with a resolvable RePORTER URL.

Careful attribution semantics: RePORTER's sole-PI designation (Eric S. Rosenthal) is kept distinct from Leadership Team membership for five other named individuals, each with a source_caveats note explaining why the person-valued principal_investigator field is left empty.
Instances are annotated with B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE ontology terms, and the 1.6-billion-row OMOP count is honestly flagged as 'a rounded figure expressed in full and ... not an exact count'.
The under-review website banner is transcribed verbatim including its typographical error ('This repoitory is under review...'), preserving evidentiary fidelity over cosmetic correction.

Temporal claims are internally consistent: the award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 brackets the August/September 2025 coverage snapshots, and retrospective collection is distinguished from the unstated calendar range of the underlying clinical encounters.

sub_elements.evidence: Learning resources on chorus4ai.org, the interactive SOP workflow diagram, the chorus-developer web guide, the AIM-AHEAD cohort 2 informational webinar, and hands-on training with canonical Jupyter Notebooks and the OHDSI tool stack in intended_uses
sub_elements.quality_note: Extensive training and documentation ecosystem documented.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.evidence: No related_datasets field
sub_elements.quality_note: No typed relationships to related datasets (e.g., the three sibling Bridge2AI data-generation projects, or MIMIC/eICU as prior critical-care corpora).

strengths: Exceptional source transparency and conflict reconciliation: source_caveats resolves the 50,000-vs-45,000+ admission count by explicit source tiering, flags that radiology-admission and image counts 'count different units', discloses that the garbled webinar modality table forced two column-order-only attributions, scopes the MIT license to software rather than data, and transcribes a typo'd contact email and website banner verbatim with explicit flags rather than silently correcting them.

Complete technical transparency (Element 8, 5/5): per-modality collection mechanisms, acquisition methods with correct observed/derived/validated provenance flags, a six-step preprocessing pipeline with named tools (chorus-mapping, OHNLP, DeGauss, CTP-deid, waveform conversion scripts), and a cleaning feedback loop via per-site characterization reports.

Full motivation and funding transparency (Element 7, 5/5) with a format-valid NIH award number (OT2OD032701 / 1OT2OD032701-01) used consistently and cross-referenced to RePORTER, plus careful PI-versus-leadership attribution across six named individuals.
Strong standards interoperability: OMOP CDM (with flowsheet extensions), DICOM, WFDB, EDF+, Persyst and OHNLP conformance declared, with the OTHER enum value explicitly expanded in prose.

Modality-appropriate privacy engineering documented: text tokenization with local note retention, imaging de-identification, re-identification-limiting transforms, and controlled enclave access, applied to an at-risk population that explicitly includes minors and neonates.
weaknesses: No persistent identifier: no DOI or RRID, the id is a self-minted website fragment (admitted in source_caveats), no publisher is asserted, and no citable publication exists — the dataset is hard to cite or cross-reference despite being released.

Ethics documentation gaps for a human-subjects dataset that includes minors: no IRB approval number or reviewing committee, and no informed-consent or consent-waiver documentation — both honestly flagged as source gaps but still failing the human-subjects consistency expectations.
Version tracking is nearly absent (Element 6, 2/5): no version number, no version access method, no errata or changelog, and no formal release date for a dataset already in use by training cohorts.
No variable-level metadata or data dictionary for ~1.6 billion OMOP rows; per-modality metadata-schema status could not even be asserted from the sources.

Reuse permissions are opaque: the licensing agreement's substantive terms are not summarized, and no related_datasets relationships situate CHoRUS among sibling Bridge2AI or prior critical-care datasets.
recommendations: Mint a DOI for the released dataset (and consider an RRID), and assert a publisher, so the enclave-hosted resource becomes citable and cross-referenceable.

Document the IRB/ethics approvals or waiver determinations covering the 14 data-acquisition hospitals, including the consent basis (likely a waiver for retrospective records) and its application to PICU/NICU admissions.
Introduce explicit release versioning with a changelog and formal release dates; record how users pin or reference a specific enclave release.
Publish or link variable-level metadata: the OMOP tables and flowsheet extensions in use, and the per-modality metadata schemas as they move from planned to published.
Summarize the substantive terms of the data licensing agreement (permitted uses, publication rights, re-identification prohibition, enclave export policy) in license_and_use_terms.
Add related_datasets entries with typed relationships — at minimum the sequestered holdout's relationship to the main dataset, sibling Bridge2AI datasets, and antecedent critical-care corpora.
